newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFrica's Hosken says in talks.
newsitem.headline: SAFrica's Hosken says in talks.

text.p: South African group Hosken Consolidated Investments Limited (HCI) said on Monday that it was involved in talks which could have an impact on its share price.
The firm said shareholders should exercise caution in their dealings in its shares until further details are announced.
In January the firm said its board of directors had been reconstituted to include former trade union leaders and MPs Marcel Golding and John Copelyn.
This follows the acquisition of a controlling stake in HCI by the investment arms of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and the South African Clothing and Textile Workers Union (SACTWU).
Golding and Copelyn are key figures behind the establishment of the NUM's Mineworkers' Investment Company and SACTWU Investments -- which have emerged as important players in black empowerment deals.
